questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Porous wood has abundance of
questions.solution: Porous wood possesses abundant vessels. Due to the presence of vessels, they are called porous woods.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Velamen is a specialized tissue found in
questions.solution: Velamen is a dead spongy tissue present in epiphytic roots (hygroscopic roots). With the help of velamen, these roots are able to absorb water from moist atmosphere, dew and rain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Monocot stem bears collateral open vascular bundles.
Reason : If cambium is absent such vascular bundles are called closed type.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: Monocot stem bears collateral closed vascular bundle. In monocot stem cambium is absent and such vasular bundle is called closed type.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Class Crustacea has following features :
options: Head and thorax, biramous appendages, book lungs
Head and thorax, book lungs, chitinous exoskeleton
questions.solution: Crustaceans are mostly marine but a few live in freshwater or moist places. Body consists of cephalothorax and abdomen. Each body segment bears a pair of biramous appendages. Respiration occurs through body surface or gills. Excretion occurs through green glands. They bear two pairs of antennae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about nematocyst?
options: It is excretory organ in arthropods
It is ejected on contact and pierce the prey.
questions.solution: Nematocysts are the stinging cells and are the organs of offence and defence of coelenterates, Nematocyst contains a poisonous proteinaceous fluid hypnotoxin along tube which injects the fluid into the victim. Nematocysts are activated in response to chemicals secreted by prey. They explode after coming in contact with the prey.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Salamander, Sphenodon are classified as amphibians.
Reason : Sphenodon is regarded as living fossil.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: Salamander is a tailed carnivorous and nocturnal amphibian. Sphenodon is a burrowing, carnivorous and nocturnal reptile. It is regarded as a living fossil.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is wrongly matched?
questions.solution: In arthropods like prawn, the blood is colourless and contains WBCs only. The blue respiratory pigment, haemocyanin is present in the blood of molluses. The RBCs of mammals contain the red pigment haemoglobin which carries oxygen.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is an egg laying mammal ?
questions.solution: Duck billed platypus is an egg laying mammal.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Among the land animals, the Cheetah can run fastest over the ground.
Reason : The Cheetah uses its powerful forelimbs to push itself forward during running.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: Cheetah is the most successful runner among quadrupedal animals. Because of its specially developed forelimbs and bodyshape, it acquires the power of fastest running over the ground. During running, it uses its powerful forelimbs to push itself forward.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The sphere of living matter together with water, air and soil on the surface of earth is called
questions.solution: Biosphere is the biologically inhabited part of earth along with its abiotic or physiochemical components. Biosphere consists of three interacting subdivisions - atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere. Atmosphere is the transparent gaseous mantle surrounding the earth. Lithosphere is the outer solid crust of earth. Hydrosphere is liquid mantle of earth.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The protists have
options: membrane bound nucleoproteins lying embedded in the cytoplasm.
nucleoprotein in direct contact with the rest of the cell substance
questions.solution: No Solution Available

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Some Gram -ve bacteria have peptidoglycan and an extra layer of
questions.solution: Cell wall is two layered and wavy in Gram (-) bacteria. The wall contains peptidoglycan in the inner layer. The outer layer has lipopolysaccharides, proteins and phospholipids.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : Plasma membrane is exceedingly thin and not visible as a separate layer.
Reason : It appears merely as a surface layer of cytoplasm.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: All cells are bounded by a thin membrane called the plasmalemma. This membrane is not seen under light microscope as separate layer. It has no cell cement and thus it is very thin. It has structural proteins, enzymes and carrier proteins.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of these are most widely used in genetic engineering?
questions.solution:
Plastids are semiautonomous cell organelles. They take part in storage and synthesis of organic compounds. Mitochondria are called the power houses of the cell as they are the centres of Kreb's cycle of respiration liberating the maximum amount of energy. Ribosomes are submicroscopic cell organelles manufacturing protein.
Plasmids are defined as autonomous elements, whose genomes exist in the cell as the extrachromosomal unit. These are the chromosomal elements found in bacteria. Plasmids are used as cloning vectors due to their increased yield potential.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During the cell cycle, DNA content is doubled in the
questions.solution: Cell cycle is a series of cyclic changes through which a cell passes during its growth and division. In the cell cycle, the resting stage or interphase can be divided into three periods.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Barr body is found in the cytoplasm during
options: interphase in cell of female mammal
interphase in cell of male mammal
prophase in cell of female mammal
prophase in cell of male mammal.
questions.solution: Barr body is also known as sex chromatin, $\mathrm{X}$ chromatin. Barr body is partially inactivated and development of this facultative heterochromatin occurs in one of the two $\mathrm{X}$ chromosomes in interphase nuclei. Any of the two $\mathrm{X}$-chromosomes can become heterochromatic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which floral family has (9) +1 arrangement of anthers in the androecium ?
questions.solution: In Fabaceae stamens have diadelphous arrangement i.e. (9) + 1. In total these are 10 in number.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Clove is a
questions.solution: Cloves are unopened floral buds of Syzygium aromaticum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Coconut's husk fibre, coir of commerce is extracted from
questions.solution: Commercial coir is obtained from the fibrous husk (mesocarp) of fruits of coconut palm. The fibre is valued for its lightness and exceedingly high resistance to mechanical wear and dampness.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During formation of which of the following free nuclear division occurs?
questions.solution: In nuclear endosperm the primary endosperm nucleus divides repeatedly without wall formation producing a large number of free nuclei. It is most common type of endosperm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following pesticides is an acetylcho linesterase inhibitor?
questions.solution: Organophosphate (Malathion) kills insects by inhibiting enzyme cholinesterase. It is organic ester of carbonic acid. In structure, it is quite similar to acetylcholine and, therefore has strong affinity for the enzyme acetylcholinesterase, and inhibits its activity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct regarding short day plants (SDPs)?
options: They can flower in complete darkness if supplied with exogenous nutrients.
They are the same as long day plants.
They do not have a critical photoperiod.
questions.solution: No Solution Available

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Induction of flowering by low temperature in plants is
questions.solution: Vernalization is a process of shortening of the juvenile or vegetative phase and hastening flowering by a previous cold treatment. The term vernalization was coined by Lysenko (1928).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Wooden doors swell up and get stuck during the rainy season. This is due to the phenomenon of
questions.solution: Jamming of wooden frames during rains is caused by swelling of wood due to imbibition. (The absorption of water by the solid particles of a substance without forming a solution is called imbibition).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Stomata opens
options: in day time - for gaseous exchange
in day time - no gaseous exchange
in night time only - for gaseous exchange
in night time only - no gaseous exchange.
questions.solution: Stomata are meant for gaseous exchange but are also the main source of transpiration. In majority of plants stomata open in the presence of light i.e., in daytime and close in darkness (night).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Assertion : A plant girdled upto bast will die. 
Reason : Food transportation in such plant will cease followed by ceasation of water transport.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explantion of Assertion
If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
If Assertion is true but Reason is false
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: A plant girdled upto bast will show below the girdled part, the non transportation of the food which occurs through phloem (bast). Water transport from roots to other plant parts via xylem will continue till root cells do not die due to starvation.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A human RBC is placed in $1.5 \%$ salt solution. It will
questions.solution: For human $\mathrm{RBC}, 0.9 \%$ salt solution is isotonic. Hence a medium of $1.5 \%$ salt solution would be hypertonic i.e. more concentrated. Hence, the RBC will shrink due to exosmosis.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In plants, water moves from
options: less negative to more negative potential
more negative to less negative potential
questions.solution: Water always moves from the area of high water potential to the area of low water potential i.e., from less negative potential to more negative potential.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following option w.r.t. increasing bond order is correct ?

Bond order of the molecules :

\mathrm{O}_2^{-}: K K(\sigma 2 s)^2\left(\sigma_2 *\right)^2\left(\sigma 2 p_{\mathrm{z}}\right)^2\left(\pi 2 p_{\mathrm{x}}\right)^2\left(\pi 2 p_{\mathrm{y}}\right)^2\left(\pi^* 2 p_x\right)^2\left(\pi^* 2 p_y\right)^1

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Hybridisation in $\mathrm{CH}_3, \stackrel{+}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3$ and $\overline{\mathrm{C}}_3$ are respectively
questions.solution:
$\dot{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{H}_3$ (methyl free radical) has planar structure with $s p^2$ hybridisation of ' $\mathrm{C}$ ' atom. The odd electron is present in unhybridised $2 p_z$ orbital.
$\oplus\mathrm{CH}_3$ (methyl carbonium ion) has also trigonal planar structure $\left(s p^2\right)$.
$\stackrel{\ominus}{\mathrm{CH}_3}$ (methyl carbanion) has tetrahedral structure $\left(s p^3\right)$ and one of the hybrid orbitals contains the lone pair of electrons.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In which of the following $p \pi-d \pi$ bonding is possible?
questions.solution:
Carbon, oxygen and nitrogen atoms do not have any $d$-orbital available. Therefore, in $\mathrm{CO}_3^{2-}, \mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$ and $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$, there is no possibility of $p \pi-d \pi$ type of bonding.
In $\mathrm{PO}_4{ }^{3-}$ phosphorus atom has vacant $d$-orbital available which is used to form $p \pi-d \pi$ type of bonding with $p$-orbital of oxygen atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The $\mathrm{BCl}_3$ is a planar molecule where as $\mathrm{NCl}_3$ is pyramidal, because
options: $\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is more polar than $\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond
$\mathrm{N}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond is more covalent than $\mathrm{B}-\mathrm{Cl}$ bond
nitrogen atom is smaller than boron atoms
$\mathrm{BCl}_3$ has no lone pair but $\mathrm{NCl}_3$ has a lone pair of electrons.
questions.solution:
No lone pair of electron is available in $\mathrm{BCl}_3$.
One lone pair of electron is available on N-atoms, it occupies a corner in the tetrahedral arrangement. Therefore, $\mathrm{NCl}_3$ appears pyramidal in shape.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : $o$-Nitrophenol is more volatile than $p$-nitrophenol.
Reason : Intramolecular hydrogen bonding is present in $o$-nitrophenol while intermolecular $\mathrm{H}$ - bonding is in $p$-nitrophenol.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: p-Nitrophenol has higher boiling point than o-nitrophenol, because intermolecular hydrogen bonding present in $p$-nitrophenol is responsible for it. But intramolecular hydrogen bonding in $o$-nitrophenol does not effect boiling point.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}$ are miscible.
Reason : One of them is polar.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ and $\mathrm{CH}_3-\mathrm{OH}$ are miscible due to intermolecular van der Waals force of attraction. However, $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OH}$ and $\mathrm{CHCl}_3$ are polar molecules.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OCH}_3$ and $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ has comparable molecular weight but boiling point of $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ is more than dimethyl ether.
Reason : $\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}$ forms intermolecular Hbonding while $\mathrm{CH}_3 \mathrm{OCH}_3$ forms intramolecular $\mathrm{H}$-bonding.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: Due to the presence of hydroxyl group $(-\mathrm{OH})$, there is extensive hydrogen bonding between the ethanol molecules $\left(\mathrm{C}_2 \mathrm{H}_5 \mathrm{OH}\right)$. But there is no such hydrogen bonding in dimethyl ether (due to absence of -OH group). So boiling point of dimethyl ether is much lower than ethanol.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$ is soluble in water while $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ is not.
Reason : Lattice energy of $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ exceeds its hydration energy.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: The large sized sulphate anion $\left(\mathrm{SO}_4{ }^{2-}\right)$ is stabilised better by a large sized cation. So the stability of sulphates down the group increases so the lattice energy is more in $\mathrm{BaSO}_4$ than in $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following has highest second ionization energy?
questions.solution:
Electronic configuration for chromium is :

{ }_{24} \mathrm{Cr} \rightarrow 1 s^2 2 s^2 2 p^6 3 s^2 3 p^6 3 d^5 4 s^1

After ionisation of $4 s$ electron the next electron which will be ionised is from $3 d$ orbital. As $3 d^5$ electronic configuration, is stable, hence, the second ionisation of $\mathrm{Cr}$ will require much greater ionisation energy than the expected one.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Smallest intermolecular distance is found in
questions.solution:
In $\mathrm{O}_2$, the bond order $=2$
In $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$, the bond order $=2.5$
In $\mathrm{O}_2^{-}$, the bond order $=1.5$
In $\mathrm{O}_2^{-2}$, the bond order $=1$
As the bond order in $\mathrm{O}_2^{+}$is highest, so its internuclear distance is smallest.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6, \mathrm{Si}_2 \mathrm{H}_6$ are said to have similar structure.
Reason : They have same number of $\sigma$ and $\pi$ bonds .
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.

If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution: $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6$ is an electron deficient compound. $\mathrm{B}_2 \mathrm{H}_6$ contain some unusual bonds which are called as 2 -electron 3 -centre bonds.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is a characteristic of a reversible reaction?
options: It can be influenced by a catalyst
It proceeds only in forward direction
Number of moles of reactants and products are equal.
questions.solution: Reversible reactions are those reaction in which there is equilibrium established at every infinitesimal step. But the rate of forward and rate of backward reaction can be influenced (or speed up) by the use of catalyst.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : Hydrogen nuclei combines to form helium nuclei then energy is released.
Reason : Binding energy/nucleon of He is greater than hydrogen.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Anuclear reaction in which two lighter nuclei are fused together to form a heavier nuclei is called nuclear fusion. In such a process, more stable nuclei come into existence i.e., binding energy per nucleon increases. Fusionreactionsarehighlyexothermicbecause of loss of mass during fusion. e.g.

{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H}+{ }_1^2 \mathrm{H} \rightarrow{ }_2^4 \mathrm{He}+24.9 \mathrm{MeV}

questions.q: The number of moles of electrons required to deposit $1 \mathrm{~g}$ equivalent aluminium (atomic wt. $=27$ ) from a solution of aluminium chloride will be
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Al}^{3+}+3 e^{-} \rightarrow \mathrm{Al}$
Therefore, number of moles of electrons required to deposite $1 \mathrm{gm}$ equivelent of aluminium is three.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: When the temperature of reactions will increase then the effect on $\mathrm{pH}$ value will
questions.solution: As the temperature increases, the dissociation of water in solution increases. Hence the $\mathrm{H}^{+}$ion conc. increases and $\mathrm{pH}$ of the solution decreases with increase in temperature.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is strongest Bronsted base?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{HClO}_4$ is the strongest acid among $\mathrm{HClO}$, $\mathrm{HClO}_2, \mathrm{HClO}_3$ and $\mathrm{HClO}_4$ as more the number of oxygen atoms attached, more is the acidity of the molecule order of acidity is :

\mathrm{HClO} < \mathrm{HClO}_2 < \mathrm{HClO}_3 < \mathrm{HClO}_4

So the conjugate base order will be just the reverse:

\mathrm{ClO}^{-}>\mathrm{ClO}_2^{-}>\mathrm{ClO}_3^{-}>\mathrm{ClO}_4^{-}

The $\mathrm{pH}$ of aqueous solution of ammonium formate is
$\left(\mathrm{p} K_a\right.$ of $\mathrm{HCOOH}=3.8$ and $\mathrm{p} K_b$ of $\left.\mathrm{NH}_3=4.8\right)$

& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{10^{-2}}{10^{-6}}=10^4=10,000 \\
&

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following hydrogen halides is most basic?
questions.solution: The bond strength $\mathrm{H}-X$ decreases from $\mathrm{HF}$ to HI. Thus HF is the most stable and hence weakest acid while is least stable and most acidic. In aqueous solutions, $\mathrm{HF}$ is only slightly ionised but $\mathrm{HCl}, \mathrm{HBr}$ and HI are almost completely ionised. As basicity is the reverse of acidity. Therefore, $\mathrm{HF}$ is the most basic of all $\mathrm{H}-X$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which one forms $\mathrm{KHX}_2$ type compound?
questions.solution:
Hydrogen fluoride is an associated molecule and can be represented by $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2$. This is due to the fact that strong hydrogen bonding exists between the molecules. (as $\mathrm{F}$ is highly electronegative element)

\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{~F}_2+\mathrm{KF} \rightarrow \mathrm{KHF}_2+\mathrm{HF}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Assertion : In some cases oxygen shows positive oxidation number though it is an electronegative element.
Reason : Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen.
options: If both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
If both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
If Assertion is true but Reason is false.
If Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
Oxygen is the most electronegative element after fluorine. Therefore, in the compounds between oxygen and fluorine, oxygen is found to show positive oxidation state.
e.g. $\mathrm{OF}_2$ : Oxygen difluoride.
Oxidation state of oxygen here is +2 .

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solid $A B$ has $\mathrm{NaCl}$ type structure. The radius of $A^{+}$is $100 \mathrm{pm}$. What is the radius of $B^{-}$?
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{NaCl}$ type structure is also called face centred cubic lattice. Here the radius ratio $\left(r_c / r_a\right)$ ranges from 0.414 to 0.732 .

\begin{aligned}
\text { Radius ratio }=\frac{r_c}{r_a}= & \frac{\text { radius of cation }}{\text { radius of anion }} \\
\Rightarrow \quad \text { Radius of anion }\left(B^{-}\right) & =\frac{\text { radius of } A^{+}}{\text {radius ratio }} \\
& =\frac{100}{0.414} \text { to } \frac{100}{0.732} \\
& =241.5 \text { to } 136.6 .
\end{aligned}

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Crystalline solids have
questions.solution: Crystalline solids are anisotropic therefore their physical properties e.g. electrical conductivity, thermal conductivity, refractive index are the different in different directions. But amorphous solids, liquids and gases are isotropic (i.e. same physical properties in all directions).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Vapour pressure of benzene at $30^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ is $121.8 \mathrm{~mm}$. When $15 \mathrm{~g}$ of a non-volatile solute is dissolved in $250 \mathrm{~g}$ of benzene, its vapour pressure is decreased to $120.2 \mathrm{~mm}$. The molecular weight of the solute is
questions.solution:
Relative lowering of vapour pressure is given by :

\frac{P^0-P}{P^0}=\frac{w / m}{w / m+W / M}

Where, $P^0=$ Vapour pressure of pure solvent
$P=$ Vapour pressure of solution
$w$ mass of solute
$m=$ molecular mass of solute
$W$ = mass of solvent
$M=$ molecular mass of solvent.
For dilute solution

\Rightarrow \quad \frac{121.8-120.2}{121.8}=\frac{15 / m}{250 / 78} \Rightarrow m=356.265

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: How many litres of ammonia gas at S.T.P. would be needed to prepare $100 \mathrm{~mL}$ of $2.5 \mathrm{M}$ ammonium hydroxide solution?
questions.solution:
Molecular weight of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}=35$
Now, $35 \mathrm{~g}$ of $\mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ is needed to prepare $1 \mathrm{M}$ solution in 1 litre
$\Rightarrow 35 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ in $1 \mathrm{~L}$ solution $\equiv 1$ molar solution
$\Rightarrow 2.5 \times 35 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}$ in $1 \mathrm{~L}$ solution $\equiv 2.5$ molar solution

\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \frac{2.5 \times 35}{10} \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \text { is } 100 \mathrm{~mL} \text { solution } \equiv 2.5 \text { molar solution } \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 8.75 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \text { was dissolved. } \\
& \mathrm{NH}_3+\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH} \\
& \quad \text { For } 35 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}, \mathrm{NH}_3 \text { needed }=22.4 \mathrm{~L} \text { at S.T.P } \\
& \Rightarrow \quad \text { for } 8.75 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{NH}_4 \mathrm{OH}, \mathrm{NH}_3 \text { needed }=\frac{22.4}{35} \times 8.75 \mathrm{~L} \\
&=5.6 \mathrm{~L}

questions.q: Which of the following is always feasible?
options: $\Delta H$ (+ve), $T \Delta S$ (-ve) and $\Delta H \gt T \Delta S$
$\Delta H$ (-ve), $T \Delta S$ (+ve) and $\Delta H \lt  T \Delta S$
$\Delta H$ (-ve), $T \Delta S$ (-ve) and $\Delta H \gt T \Delta S$.
questions.solution:
Feasibility of reaction is determined by free energy change value $(\Delta G) . \Delta G$ is given by Gibbs - Helmholtz equation :

\Delta G=\Delta H-T \Delta S

Reaction is feasible if $\Delta G$ value is negative. Therefore, if $\Delta H$ is negative and $T \Delta S$ is positive then the $\Delta G$ will always be feasible.

questions.q: If in a circuit current lags behind EMF by $\pi / 2$. Then it is a/an
questions.solution: Figure shows a purely inductive circuit, in which a sinusoidal emf is applied. The induced emf across the inductor is - $L \frac{d i}{d t}$ so that from Kirchhoff's law, \begin{aligned} & \varepsilon_0 \sin \omega t-L \frac{d i}{d t}=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d i}{d t}=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{L} \sin \omega t \\ & \text { or } i=-\frac{\varepsilon_0}{\cos } \cos \omega t+C \end{aligned} The constant $C$ can be shown to be zero from the fact that, the emf being sinusoidal, the current should also be so, and the average current over one time period has to be zero. \therefore i=-\frac{\varepsilon_0}{\omega L} \cos \omega \mathrm{t} \quad \text { or } i=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{\omega L} \sin (\omega \mathrm{t}-\pi / 2) which shows that the current lags behind the emf by a phase of $\pi / 2$

questions.q: A body of mass $M$ moving with velocity $V$ explodes into two equal parts. If one comes to rest and the other body moves with velocity $v$, what would be the value of $v$ ?
questions.solution: Before explosion, the total momentum of the system $=M V$ After explosion, the total momentum of the system =\frac{M}{2} \times 0+\frac{M}{2} \times v=\frac{M v}{2} From the principal of momentum conservation, \begin{aligned} & M V=\frac{M v}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad & v=2 V \end{aligned}

questions.q: A body weighed $250 \mathrm{~N}$ on the surface assuming the earth to be a sphere of uniform mass density, how much would it weigh half way down to the centre of the earth?
questions.solution: At a depth $d$ below the surface of the earth, \begin{aligned} & m g^{\prime}=G \frac{M^{\prime} m}{(R-d)^2} \\ & M^{\prime}=\frac{4}{3} \pi(R-d)^3 \rho \end{aligned} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad g^{\prime} & =\frac{G M^{\prime}}{(R-d)^2} \\ & =\frac{4}{3} G \pi(R-d) \rho \end{aligned} If $\quad d=\frac{R}{2}$ then g^{\prime}=\frac{4}{3} G \pi \rho=\frac{2 \pi G R \rho}{3} On the surface of the earth \begin{aligned} g & =\frac{G m}{R V}=\frac{4}{3} \pi G R \rho \\ \therefore \quad g^{\prime} & =\frac{g}{2} \end{aligned} $\therefore$ The body weighed $250 \mathrm{~N}$ on the surface of the earth would weigh $\frac{1}{2} \times 250=125 \mathrm{~N}$, half way down towards the centre of the earth.

questions.q: Two masses are attached to a rod end to end. If torque is applied they rotate with angular acceleration $\alpha$. If their distances are doubled and same torque is applied, then they move with angular acceleration
questions.solution: Suppose the masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are attached to the ends of a massless rod. $C_1$ is the axis of rotation which is at a distance $R$ from each of the masses. $\therefore$ the moment of inertia of the system, \mathrm{I}=m_1 R^2+m_2 R^2=\left(m_1+m_2\right) R^2 Now if the distance between the masses is doubled, then the moment of inertia \Gamma=m_1(2 R)^2+m_2(2 R)^2=\left(m_1+m_2\right) 4 R^2 Since the same torque is applied in both the cases, \begin{aligned} & \tau=I \alpha=I^{\prime} \alpha^{\prime} \\ & \Rightarrow \alpha^{\prime}=\frac{I \alpha}{I^{\prime}}=\frac{\left(m_1+m_2\right) R^2 \alpha}{\left(m_1+m_2\right) 4 R^2}=\frac{\alpha}{4} \end{aligned}

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.q: Some students, during a study, caught, marked and released 80 fishes in a pond. Later 100 fishes were caught at random. Among these 40 were found to be marked. What is the approximate number of fishes in the pond?
questions.solution:
According to Petersons Mark and Recapture Method, the population (P) is given by

P=m(r+u) / r

where $m=$ number of marked fishes
$r=$ number of marked fishes recaptured
$u=$ number of unmarked fishes captured
Here,

\begin{aligned}
m & =80 \\
r & =40 \\
u & =(100-40) \\
& =60 \\
P & =\mathrm{m}(\mathrm{r}+\mathrm{u}) / \mathrm{r} \\
& =\frac{80(40+60)}{40} \\
P & =200
\end{aligned}
